about.title: About
paragraphs: Offerfy is a web resume editor at https://offerfy.cc. You keep a Typst source file in the browser. Chat can edit that same file. The PDF preview updates from the compile. This is not a generate-and-download product. You can start without creating an account.

We also publish a public job catalog from official employer ATS boards (Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby) and TaiwanJobs open data. Offerfy does not scrape 104 or LinkedIn. When you apply, you leave Offerfy and use the original posting. We do not match your resume to jobs, tailor a resume to a listing, or submit applications for you.
The homepage sells the editor first. Featured listings are real open roles from that catalog. Contact is james@offerfy.cc. There is no public office address.

contact.metaDescription: Email james@offerfy.cc. Offerfy has no public office and no self-serve API keys.
contact.title: Contact
paragraphs: Email james@offerfy.cc for product questions, privacy requests, and signed-in data deletion. There is no public office, no phone desk, and no in-app staff chat.

Google sign-in is for people using the website. There is no self-serve API key, OAuth authorization server for machines, or agent sandbox. Guest use of the editor is rate-limited in production to protect compile and chat.
Questions about the public jobs catalog — what we ingest, and that apply happens on the source site — can go to the same address. We do not apply, match, or tailor on your behalf.

terms.title: Terms of Service
terms.intro: These Terms of Service describe how you may use Offerfy at https://offerfy.cc. They describe current Phase 1 practices. They are not legal advice.

sections.heading: Who we are
paragraphs: Offerfy operates the website at https://offerfy.cc. These pages list the product name only; there is no separate company legal name here. Contact us at james@offerfy.cc.

sections.heading: The service
paragraphs: Offerfy is a web resume editor. You can create a resume from a starter template or upload a file, edit Typst source, preview a live compile, export a PDF, and check whether that compiled PDF can be parsed by applicant tracking systems (ATS).
ATS checks parseability of the compiled PDF only. They do not predict hireability or job outcomes.
You may use the editor without an account. Signing in with Google saves your resume history.

Offerfy also publishes a public job catalog collected from employer career-board APIs (Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby) and TaiwanJobs open data. Applying happens on the original posting. We do not operate 104 or LinkedIn. If you turn on “Open to matching” in your settings, we may introduce you to employers; the Privacy Policy explains what is passed on. We still do not score your resume against a posting, tailor it to one, or track your applications.

sections.heading: Accounts
paragraphs: If you use Offerfy without signing in, we set an offerfy_guest cookie so an anonymous session can own your resumes.
If you sign in with Google, we request the openid, email, and profile scopes. We store your Google subject identifier and email so we can keep you signed in and attach resumes to your account.

sections.heading: Your content
paragraphs: You retain rights in the resumes, uploads, and chat messages you provide.

You grant Offerfy a license to host that content, compile it, generate previews and PDFs, run ATS parseability checks, and — only when you use chat — send relevant content to our language-model provider so we can operate the service.
You are responsible for the accuracy of your resume and for having the right to upload any file you provide.

sections.heading: Acceptable use
paragraphs: Do not abuse the service, upload malware, attempt to disrupt or overload it, scrape it in a way that harms availability, or use it to process personal data you have no right to process.

sections.heading: AI
paragraphs: Chat is optional. You can edit Typst without ever opening chat.
Model output can be wrong or incomplete. You must review any AI-edited resume before you use it.

AI editing has a weekly allowance, which depends on whether you have an account and whether you have turned on “Open to matching”. Editing Typst by hand, the live preview, PDF export and ATS checks are not limited at any tier. The current figures are at offerfy.cc/usage, linked below.

Turning on “Open to matching” comes with a larger weekly allowance as thanks. It is not required in order to use Offerfy: the signed-in allowance is intended to be sufficient on its own. You may turn matching off at any time, we will not reclaim allowance you have already used, and nothing you have created is affected.

There is also an hourly cap to prevent one account from spending the service's budget at once, and a cap on what Offerfy as a whole spends on AI each week. If the latter is reached, AI editing pauses for everyone until the week resets; everything else keeps working.

sections.heading: Availability
paragraphs: Offerfy is provided as-is. Phase 1 is an early product. We do not promise uptime, backups, or that features will remain unchanged.

sections.heading: Liability
paragraphs: To the extent permitted by applicable law, Offerfy is not liable for indirect, incidental, special, or consequential damages, or for lost opportunities, arising from your use of the service.

Our total liability for claims relating to the service is limited to the amount you paid us for the service in the 12 months before the claim. Phase 1 is provided without charge, so that amount is currently zero.
Some jurisdictions do not allow certain limitations. Those limits apply only to the extent the law allows.

sections.heading: Changes
paragraphs: We may update these terms. The date at the top is the latest version. If you keep using Offerfy after a change, you accept the updated terms.

sections.heading: Governing law
paragraphs: These terms are governed by the laws of Taiwan (Republic of China), without regard to conflict-of-law rules.

sections.heading: Contact
paragraphs: Questions about these terms: james@offerfy.cc.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: This Privacy Policy describes how Offerfy collects and uses personal data on https://offerfy.cc. It describes current Phase 1 practices. It is not legal advice.

sections.heading: Who we are
paragraphs: Offerfy operates https://offerfy.cc. We process personal data to run the service. Contact: james@offerfy.cc.

sections.heading: What we collect
paragraphs: Guest use: we set an offerfy_guest cookie (HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Secure in production). We store a guest session, the resumes attached to it, and rate-limit events in our database.

Signed-in use: when you sign in with Google we receive identifiers from the openid, email, and profile scopes. We store your Google subject identifier, email, and locale, and we set an offerfy_session cookie (HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Secure in production).
Language: we set an offerfy_locale cookie so the site stays in the language you chose.
Theme: light/dark preference is stored in the browser with localStorage. It is not a cookie.
Resume data: title, Typst source, compiled SVG and PDF, ATS parseability report, and chat messages.
Uploads: PDF, PNG, JPG, JPEG, WEBP, TXT, and MD files, up to 10 MiB, stored in object storage.
Job catalog: we store copies of public job postings from employer ATS board APIs and TaiwanJobs open data so we can show the catalog. These listings are not your personal data.

Usage metering: for each model call we record what it billed — token counts, the model name and a cost figure — attached to your account or guest session, so the weekly allowance can be enforced. We also record when a request was refused for reaching a limit, with the tier and which limit it was. Neither record contains your resume, your uploads or your messages.

sections.heading: Why we use it
paragraphs: We use this data to provide the editor, live preview, PDF export, ATS parseability checks, the public job catalog, authentication, guest rate limits, and the language you selected.

sections.heading: Talent introduction (only if you turn it on)
paragraphs: If you explicitly turn on “Open to matching” in your settings, we pass your resume data to hiring companies, or to recruiters acting for them, to introduce you to roles.
This is off by default. Until you turn it on, we give your resume to no employer. You can turn it off at any time; we then stop passing it on and require anyone who already has it to stop using it.

What we pass on is a short profile built from the published version of a resume you choose — roles, skills, education, and a summary. It never includes your email, phone number, or links; if an employer is interested, Offerfy introduces you. We record every read of your profile and who read it, and you can see that count in your settings.

sections.heading: When we share
paragraphs: Google: to sign you in.

Language-model provider: we send resume, upload, and chat content to an OpenAI-compatible API when you use chat, and — if you have turned on “Open to matching” — to build the profile we show employers.
Employers and recruiters: only if you have turned on “Open to matching”, and only through credentials we issue to named organisations. There is no public or self-serve access.
Infrastructure: database, object storage, and hosting that run Offerfy.
We do not sell personal data. Offerfy does not include a third-party analytics product today.

sections.heading: Retention
paragraphs: Guest data is tied to the offerfy_guest cookie. If you lose that cookie, you lose access to that anonymous session.
Signed-in data is kept until you ask us to delete it. There is no in-app account or data deletion yet. Email james@offerfy.cc to request deletion.
Usage metering and refusal records are kept for 90 days and then deleted. The weekly counters themselves are kept only as long as the window they belong to, plus a short grace period.

sections.heading: Your rights
paragraphs: You may ask us for access to, correction of, or deletion of personal data we hold about you by emailing james@offerfy.cc. We will handle requests in line with Taiwan's Personal Data Protection Act as it applies to us. These pages do not claim GDPR or CCPA compliance that we have not implemented.

sections.heading: Children
paragraphs: Offerfy is not directed at children under 13. The product does not include an age gate.

sections.heading: International processing
paragraphs: Google and the language-model provider may process data on servers outside Taiwan.

sections.heading: Cookies
paragraphs: We use these essential cookies to run the service. There is no cookie banner because we do not use non-essential tracking cookies.

Keeps you signed in after Google.

usage.metaDescription: What you get on Offerfy, what the AI limits are, and why they exist.
usage.title: How usage works
usage.intro: Offerfy is free. One part of it costs us real money every time you use it, so that one part has a weekly limit. This page explains exactly which part, how much you get, and why.
usage.freeHeading: What has no limit at all
usage.freeIntro: None of this is metered, at any tier, with or without an account:
freeItems: Editing your resume's Typst source by hand, as much as you like.
The live preview, and recompiling as often as you want.
ATS parseability checks on the compiled PDF.
Browsing and searching the job catalog.
usage.whyHeading: Why the AI has a limit
usage.whyBody: When you ask the assistant to change your resume, it reads the document, makes the edit, recompiles it and checks the result. That is several calls to a language-model provider, and we pay for every one of them. A weekly limit is what keeps Offerfy free instead of asking you for a card.
usage.tiersUnavailable: We could not load the current numbers. Rather than print a figure that might not be the one we actually enforce, we would rather show nothing — please reload.
usage.tiersNote: Without an account you get enough to see the assistant work on your own resume, but not enough to finish polishing a page — and publishing needs an account in any case. Signing in is free and takes one click.
usage.costlierHeading: What makes one edit cost more than another
usage.costlierIntro: We count what each edit actually costs us, so a small question costs you less than a big rewrite. These are the things that make an edit expensive:
costlierItems: A long resume. Every edit sends the whole document, so a three-page CV costs more per edit than a one-pager.
Switching templates, or uploading a file to import. Both rewrite the entire document rather than changing a few lines.
Questions about the rendered page — whether something wrapped, how crowded a page looks — because answering those means rendering it and looking.
An edit that produces a document which will not compile, because the assistant then has to repair it.
A long conversation on the same resume. The assistant is sent the history each time it acts.

sections.heading: How we count
paragraphs: We add up what the model calls actually billed us — the tokens going in, the tokens coming out, and the discounts we get when parts of the request are reused. We do not charge you twice for the discounted parts.
Credits are our own unit, not a currency. One credit is about what a typical edit costs. We use a unit of our own so that the allowance we publish stays the same when a provider changes its prices.
Occasionally a provider does not tell us what a call cost. When that happens we record our best estimate rather than nothing, and your usage page says how many of those there were.

sections.heading: The week, and where to watch it
paragraphs: The allowance resets every Monday at midnight, Taipei time. There is a meter above the chat box in the editor, and a fuller breakdown in your settings.
If you run out, nothing is lost. Your resumes, your edits and your published links all stay exactly as they are, and you can keep editing by hand and exporting PDFs until the week turns over.

sections.heading: Matching is a thank-you, not a toll
paragraphs: Turning on “Open to matching” lets us introduce you to employers, and it comes with a larger weekly allowance as thanks.

It is not how you unlock the product. The signed-in allowance is meant to be enough on its own to polish a resume and tailor it for a role, and if it turns out not to be, we will raise it rather than leave matching as the only way to get real use out of Offerfy.

You can turn it off at any time, in one click, and we will not take back the allowance you have already used this week. Turning it off removes your profile from the index and does not touch anything you have made.

sections.heading: Abuse limits
paragraphs: Separately from the weekly allowance there is a cap on how many edits can run in a single hour. It exists to stop one account or one script from spending the whole budget in a few minutes, and ordinary use does not come near it.

We also cap what the whole site can spend on AI in a week. If we ever reach it, AI editing pauses for everyone until the week turns over — and everything on the free list above keeps working. We would rather pause one feature honestly than quietly bill you for it.

includedItems: Editing your resume's Typst source by hand, as much as you like.
The live preview, and recompiling as often as you want.
Exporting the PDF — no watermark, no export cap.

notes.heading: So why is there a limit on AI editing at all?
notes.body: Because that is the one part that costs us money every time you use it. Each AI edit is several calls to a language-model provider, and we pay for every one. A weekly allowance is what lets the answer on this page stay $0 instead of becoming a card form. The usage page explains exactly how it is counted.

notes.heading: What we are not doing
notes.body: We are not collecting your card “for later”. We are not holding a feature back for a tier that does not exist. We are not watermarking your PDF, capping your exports, or deleting your work if you stop visiting. There is no annual discount, because there is nothing to discount.

notes.heading: Will it always be free?
notes.body: We are not going to promise that, because we cannot keep a promise about a product this young — our Terms say the same thing in less friendly language. What we can say is what is true today: nothing here costs anything, we are not planning a paywall, and if that ever changes we will say so plainly and in advance rather than quietly adding a price to this page.

notes.heading: Then what do you get out of it?
notes.body: If you turn on “Open to matching”, we may introduce you to employers, and that is the only thing we could ever be paid for. It is off by default, it is not required to use anything here, and the signed-in allowance is meant to be enough on its own. Turning it off costs you nothing you have already used.
